directions.title: Swiss editorial
directions.inspiration: Swiss modernist typography and a serious public-policy journal
directions.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: high-fidelity art-direction variant of the MAIN CivicSignal desktop research workspace.
Input image 1: edit target and functional layout reference. Keep the recognizable main screen, workflow and information architecture, but redesign the entire visual treatment using the specified inspiration below. The user explicitly requests five DIFFERENT art styles, so make this direction visually decisive and far more than a color theme. This call produces only ONE of those five directions, a single full-screen UI, not a comparison board.
Product: CivicSignal, a Canadian civic research tool that joins legislation, bills, debate citations and news headlines with source provenance. This is a desktop research workspace, not a marketing page.
Composition: one complete flat desktop viewport, landscape about 16:10, head-on, no device frame, no perspective. Preserve the broad functional composition of the reference: navigation on the far left, session list beside it, a central cited answer and evidence list, an inspector on the right, scope/date/provider toolbar above, follow-up composer below. Direction-specific proportions, panel edges, spacing, visual motifs, typography and icon treatment can change. Everything must remain readable and practically usable.
Preserve these key labels accurately: "CivicSignal"; navigation "Research", "Briefs", "Connect", "Embed", "Coverage"; "Research sessions"; "+ New research"; sessions "Housing policy", "Labour standards", "Privacy and data"; toolbar "Across Canada", "Last 7 days", "Your model · Connected".
Main prompt: "Which federal sources should I inspect on housing?"
Answer title: "Start with the evidence."
Answer: "Review the legislation, then inspect bill status and debate citations. News headlines add context and link to the publisher." Add tiny [1] [2] [3] citation markers.
Core source list, compact and readable: "Legislation — National Housing Act"; "Bills — Housing-related bills"; "Debates — House of Commons"; "News — Publisher headlines". Each has a subtle external link affordance. A small status line "Retrieved from 4 source types".
Inspector: "Source inspector"; "National Housing Act"; "Justice Laws Website"; fields "Type / Statute", "Jurisdiction / Federal", "Content / Full section text"; action "Open official source ↗"; notice "Unofficial version. Check the official source."; "Coverage" with "Federal records — Available" and "Municipal records — Not covered".
Composer: "Ask a follow-up about these sources…" with a send control and the three shortcuts "/coverage", "/in-force", "/changes".
Data constraints: no invented legal passages, politicians, or real-time facts. News is headlines and metadata only. All source links and source distinctions remain visible. Small footer must read "Design concept · Sample data" and include this direction's name.
Output: polished raster UI mockup at a high enough resolution for readable text. No external presentation mat, moodboard, explanatory paragraphs outside the application, watermarks or multiple screens. Use the reference's content and layout, but do not let its default blue styling, generic sans-serif text or panel chrome survive if they conflict with this direction.
ART DIRECTION 01: SWISS EDITORIAL.
Inspiration: Swiss International Typographic Style, a carefully typeset public-policy journal, uncompromising modernist grid.
Visual language: pure warm-white canvas, near-black ink, one assertive vermilion-red accent. Very strong typographic hierarchy in precise grotesk sans-serif, large left-aligned black headline, compact labels in tracked uppercase, tiny numerical section indices, thin horizontal black rules, tight disciplined grid, generous negative space. No serifs in this direction.
Transform the application chrome into clean typographic divisions: the navigation rail is white with a thin black edge and a red block marking Research; session list is a pale neutral column; central answer resembles the lead page of a modernist journal; evidence is a numbered four-row index with clean rules and restrained source symbols; inspector resembles a neatly typeset editorial fact box. Bold red send button, restrained red source-link arrows, almost no corner rounding, absolutely no shadows or gradients. A small oversized "01" and "SWISS EDITORIAL" can appear discreetly in the footer. It should look like a designer built the entire interface around typography and alignment, not a generic SaaS template.

ART DIRECTION 02: FINANCIAL TERMINAL.
Inspiration: an information-dense financial market terminal crossed with a professional newsroom operations console, designed for long research sessions.
Visual language: deep ink-black and graphite surfaces, crisp luminous amber information hierarchy, restrained cyan only for links and active selection, dim neutral grid lines, compact monospaced labels and a highly legible technical sans for the answer. Black almost-square panels, tiny precise separators, close spacing, rows with subtle zebra alternation, keyboard hints and crisp one-pixel icons. Use brightness hierarchy carefully so text is accessible and no clutter obscures the research.
Transform nav and session list into dark command panes. The central answer is a terminal research readout with a compact amber heading "Start with the evidence." Four evidence rows are tabular with small row numbers, source-type columns, and cyan links. The inspector resembles a docked data inspector, amber field names and white values; in-force/corpus coverage uses restrained green status text. Toolbar is dense, dark and purposeful; composer is a command-entry field with a tiny cyan caret and amber send key. Give the screen a confident operational character with no gradients, no rounded consumer chat bubbles, no sci-fi illustrations, no faux hacker text. Footer direction name "FINANCIAL TERMINAL". This should be unmistakably a different design from the white reference.

ART DIRECTION 03: CIVIC ATLAS.
Inspiration: a contemporary cartographic atlas and a beautifully designed public-land field guide.
Visual language: light parchment and chalk surfaces, forest-green ink, muted clay/copper accents, precise cartographic linework, elegant sturdy slab-serif headings, small humanist sans labels, subtle atlas grid coordinates and thin contour-line motifs ONLY in unused margins. Sophisticated, tactile and geographic, not a fake antique treasure map.
Functional re-expression: the far-left rail is forest green with light iconography; the session list resembles an atlas index with delicate locator dots. The central research pane is a warm paper sheet with the heading "Start with the evidence." in a distinctive slab serif. The evidence list has fine cartographic key symbols, small numbered locator markers and tidy horizontal dividers. The right source inspector feels like a map legend on cream: neatly divided metadata, a thin inset border, small grid-reference typography, a copper outlined official-source action. In the toolbar, make the existing "Across Canada" scope control feel like a map-lens control, while preserving the exact workflow. No giant map replacing the research; decorative contours must be faint and peripheral. Composer is a neat pale sheet with forest-green send control. Small footer label "CIVIC ATLAS". Distinctive quiet geographic identity with clean readable content; no photographic landscape or generic dashboard cards.

ART DIRECTION 04: PAPER RESEARCH DESK.
Inspiration: an archival reading room, a legal research notebook and a carefully assembled dossier of source documents.
Visual language: warm ivory uncoated paper, dark brown-black ink, restrained oxblood-red annotations, high-contrast literary serif headings, humanist sans controls, tiny typewriter-style metadata, delicate paper-edge shadows and file-tab geometry. A tactile editorial interface translated into a functional modern web app, not a photographed physical desk.
Functional re-expression: a pale linen left rail, session list as a vertical set of folder tabs with "Housing policy" selected. The central answer is a cream research sheet with a small stamped "RESEARCH NOTE" eyebrow, a beautiful serif "Start with the evidence." heading, and small oxblood superscript-like citations. The four evidence rows resemble neatly aligned bibliographic index entries with document numbers, subtle punched-index details at the margins and thin red pencil-style underlines for selected links. The source inspector is a slightly inset card like a library catalogue record, with metadata lines, a thin double rule, and a small oxblood seal-like source icon. The unofficial-version note is a quiet marginal note. Composer is an open notebook line with a strong simple send control; all controls remain digital and clear. No hands, no pens, no coffee, no photographic scenery, no chaotic collage. Small footer "PAPER RESEARCH DESK". More warm, personal and scholarly than the austere Swiss direction; unmistakably different from the default reference.

ART DIRECTION 05: MINIMALIST STUDIO.
Inspiration: a contemporary Scandinavian design studio and a calm premium desktop productivity app, with a carefully considered gallery-like canvas.
Visual language: very pale cool-lilac outer workspace, bright porcelain floating panels, deep plum-charcoal type, one confident periwinkle accent, subtle diffused shadows, generous soft corner radii, fine translucent separators, exceptionally clean rounded geometric sans-serif, quiet iconography. Soft depth and material contrast, not glossy glassmorphism or decorative gradient blobs.
Functional re-expression: navigation becomes a slim floating light panel with a soft lavender selection background; the session list is extremely spare with a periwinkle "New research" control. The central response has a large confident sans-serif heading "Start with the evidence." with ample whitespace. The four evidence rows are beautifully spaced compact rows inside one softly rounded container, avoiding a mess of nested cards. The source inspector is a calm rounded white utility panel with large line spacing, neat two-column metadata and a full-width periwinkle official-source action. Toolbar is a row of minimal pill-shaped controls with subtle depth; composer is a spacious floating white capsule with a simple circular periwinkle send button. The whole interface should feel light, serene, spacious and expertly restrained while preserving every functional area. Footer "MINIMALIST STUDIO". No serif, no dark rail, no financial density, no paper texture, no contour maps.
